A decision model answers bounded questions with probabilities instead of free text. Liquid’s decision model docs describe 3 question types: Noul: a yes/no question that returns a probability between 0 and 1. Choice: one label from a set, with a probability per label. Score: a probability-weighted position on an ordered rubric. The docs recommend decision models for routing, moderation, guardrails, triage and LLM-as-judge replacement. They recommend a language model for summarization, chat and code generation. How does d1-ultra work? Each request carries a state (the context), optional images , and 1 or more typed questions . The model evaluates every question against the same input in 1 call. The d1 API reference shows responses with output_tokens always at 0. Liquid AI team states that d1-ultra uses a larger open-weight backbone than d1 , along with heavy Liquid-specific customizations. Combined with Liquid’s decision training pipeline, the gains are largest on knowledge tasks. Liquid AI team built d1-ultra for messy cases. Its examples include spotting a circuit board defect against a spec. Another is checking a damage claim against the customer’s photo. How does d1-ultra perform on benchmarks? Liquid AI compared d1-ultra against its earlier d1 and TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14 across 112 evaluations. For teams building coding or browsing agents, this is a production-tested isolation […] The post Perplexity Open-Sources SPACE, a Firecracker MicroVM Sandbox for AI Agents appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Perplexity has open-sourced SPACE , the sandbox platform behind every task in Perplexity Computer. The Perplexity SPACE sandbox gives each agent task its own Firecracker microVM. Credentials and outbound traffic are controlled from outside that VM. The code ships under Apache 2.0 on GitHub . For teams building coding or browsing agents, this is a production-tested isolation layer they can self-host. TL;DR Size: Rust codebase, release 0.8.0 , the public baseline. HTTP API plus server-sent events. Runs on: A Linux x86_64 host with KVM , /dev/kvm , btrfs and Docker. Local Kind (Kubernetes) or direct mode. No macOS. Performance: In production, median create latency fell from 185 ms to 60 ms versus Perplexity’s previous provider. Best: 0 of 108 VM-to-host escape attempts succeeded across 9 frontier models. Worst: Before fixes, agents bypassed the egress policy in 11 of 54 partial-network runs. What is Perplexity SPACE? SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) is Perplexity’s platform for running agent code in isolated microVMs. Applications call its HTTP API to create Linux environments, run commands and stream output. A template supplies the starting filesystem. A sandbox is one instance of that template, with its own VM and writable disk. Many commands can run inside one sandbox. Perplexity’s launch thread explains the design goal. Agents run commands, install packages and call services with root inside the sandbox. The host stays outside the guest’s control. Agent work is long-running, stateful and branching, so it must survive restarts. How does SPACE isolate agents? Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel. A per-sandbox network gateway on the host enforces egress policy on every outbound connection. Secrets never enter the guest. Per Perplexity’s July engineering post , credentials are injected at the network layer. The credential store adds hierarchical scoping, rate limits and audit logging. The architecture guide splits the system into 4 parts. These are a PostgreSQL-backed API, controllers, worker services and a data plane. Worker services manage VMs, networking, volumes, templates and credentials. btrfs copy-on-write creates each root filesystem. How do pause, suspend and restore work? Sandboxes move through 4 states: running, paused, suspended and deleted. Paused: VM memory stays resident on the worker. This is not a durable snapshot. Suspended: VM memory, runtime state and root filesystem are snapshotted. Active resources are released. Idle default: sandboxes suspend after 6 hours without activity. For fast creates, Kubernetes deployments use warm pools of booted sandboxes. Single-node setups use base snapshots instead. In production, the 90th-percentile create latency dropped from 447 ms to 89 ms . Perplexity reports that 100% of Computer sessions run on SPACE. Did SPACE survive a red-team test? Perplexity’s Escaping SPACE: Part I report tested 9 models with root inside the guest. The study ran 216 runs across 2 tasks and 4 settings. Sandbox escape: 0 of 108 runs reached the host-side secret. No-network bypass: 0 of 54 runs succeeded. Partial-network bypass: 11 of 54 runs succeeded before fixes. 4 models found a path. Claude Opus 5.0, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Cyber and Kimi K3 found bypasses. The attacks used DNS spoofing and shared CDN IP addresses. Perplexity then added source-address validation through nftables. The gateway now terminates TLS and checks both SNI and HTTP host against the allowlist. In the retest, no model produced a verified bypass. The same team tested 10 third-party platforms. 8 showed at least one network-policy bypass. Perplexity disclosed the results to every affected vendor. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.</p> <p>Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy &amp; Gagosian.</p> <p>We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone &amp; Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.</p> <p>We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.</p> <h3><strong>Sanctuary Computer - Development</strong></h3> <p>At <strong><a href="https://www.sanctuary.computer/">Sanctuary Computer</a></strong> we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.</p> <p>Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.</p> <h3><strong>XXIX - Design</strong></h3> <p>When we started <strong><a href="https://www.xxix.co/">XXIX</a></strong> in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.</p> <p>We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.</p> <h3><strong>Index - Community</strong></h3> <p><strong><a href="https://www.index-space.org/">Index</a></strong> is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.</p> <p>We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.</p> <h3><strong><a href="https://feed.garden3d.net/">garden3d TK</a> — Media</strong></h3> <p>At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.</p> <p>We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.</p> <p>Plus, our partner organizations</p> <p><strong><a href="https://www.thelightphone.com/">Lightphone</a><br></strong><strong><a href="https://www.mill.com/">Mill</a><br></strong><strong><a href="https://ingredient-ai.com/">IngredientAI</a></strong></p> <h2>⛰️ The Head of Technology Role</h2> <p>The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder &amp; president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.</p> <p>You can be based anywhere.
